reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). The plan fits the request and the accepted reading. Everything it names exists in the snapshot: Remote (gh.rs:571), the stale comments at gh.rs:574-577 and 1787-1788, land_pr (1775), publish (1953), work_branch (1215), Athena::land_pr with the title and body built at 2132-2137, check_push and check_replace (pr.rs:134 and 170; check_replace is not yet called outside tests), and RunContext, produce_and_verify and verifier_snapshot in run.rs. The design holds up: the marker is written right after the push, and the lease-pinned replace goes through check_replace on both landing paths. The demonstrations would fail without the behavior. One problem stops me accepting it. Athena::go switches to GhEarly in production, and the CLI integration tests call Athena::go directly. Those tests are not deliverables, so the producer cannot change them, and at least two of them assert that no line contains "warning". Their fixtures have no GitHub origin, so with the plan as written GhEarly fails and the plan prints a warning: line. That breaks criterion 5. The plan's own risk list leaves this to the producer to "check", and open question 3 leaves it undecided. The planner needs to settle it. Findings: major: GhEarly on the Athena::go path will print a 'warning:' line in CLI tests that assert no warning appears, so cargo test fails (criterion 5).
